_doc: Training data recipe — 'Broad Brain' mix v3 (Expanded Verticals).
Goal: train a small model (50M-350M params) to handle code, math,
reasoning, real-world problem solving, business, marketing, psychology,
wealth/investing, motivation, fitness, UI/UX, web3 — while keeping the
persona on top via --corpus and --distill-corpus weights.
HONEST DATASET-AVAILABILITY NOTE:
Many of these verticals (dark psychology, crypto futures, wealth
creation, fitness coaching) don't have dedicated, clean, free training
datasets on HuggingFace. What DOES exist and is excellent: broad
high-quality instruction-following datasets (OpenHermes-2.5, SlimOrca,
OpenAssistant/oasst1, UltraChat) that internally cover thousands of
topics organically because they're curated from internet-scale chat.
Sales, marketing, psychology, business, motivation, even fitness and
basic investing show up naturally in those mixes. We rely on them for
vertical coverage rather than trying to find specialised single-topic
datasets that mostly don't exist.
For UI/UX we add HTML and CSS slices of The Stack — gives the model
the visual-design vocabulary it would otherwise lack.
For web3 / crypto code we already have Solidity from The Stack;
for crypto investing knowledge specifically there's no good free
training corpus — the LLM router (Groq + Gemini Flash) covers that
via the live web-search connector instead.
'Dark psychology' / manipulation tactics: NO dataset for this, and
no plan to add one — bad target for a public-revision model.
DEPLOY PATHS
Local home-11gb training:
bash scripts/train/run-home-max.sh \
--resume --variant home-11gb \
--batch 2 --grad-accum 4 --no-compile \
--mix-config scripts/data/mix-broadbrain.json
GitHub Actions daily small-variant training:
Auto-fires at 03:00 UTC every day via .github/workflows/pretrain.yml.
Each run resumes from the previous day's checkpoint on HF small-weekly.
SYNTHETIC vs HUMAN DATA
Several entries below are SYNTHETIC (generated by larger LLMs as
instruction data — OpenHermes, MetaMath, MathInstruct, Magicoder,
UltraInteract, UltraChat, SlimOrca). This is the standard small-LLM
distillation recipe — Phi-3, DeepSeek, every modern <1B model uses it.
The human-curated ones (dolly, no_robots, oasst1) provide quality
anchoring. Remove the synthetic entries if you want a pure-human-data
build (capability drops ~60%; persona stays clean).
COVERAGE MATRIX
• Persona voice:           distill-corpus + base-corpus
• Narrative warmup:        TinyStories
• Human-written quality:   dolly + no_robots + oasst1
• Broad assistant chat:    OpenHermes-2.5 + SlimOrca + UltraChat
(covers sales / marketing / psychology /
business / wealth / motivation / fitness
organically across millions of examples)
• Code Python:             the-stack-python + code-alpaca + magicoder
• Code TypeScript / JS:    the-stack-typescript
• Code Solidity / web3:    the-stack-solidity
• UI / UX / web design:    the-stack-html + the-stack-css
• Math:                    MetaMathQA + MathInstruct
• Reasoning / STEM:        Open-Platypus + UltraInteract
TOTAL POOL ≈ 60M tokens. At 20k steps/day × batch 4 × seq 2048 = 160M
tokens seen per day. Over a month: 4.8B tokens seen. That's 80 epochs
over the diverse pool — high but acceptable for instruction tuning at
small scale.

sources.name: tinystories
sources.note: Narrative warmup. Helps embeddings stabilise.

sources.name: dolly
sources.note: Human-written instructions + responses.

sources.name: no-robots
sources.note: 10K examples human-curated by skilled annotators. Zero synthetic. Highest instruction quality per token.

sources.name: oasst1
sources.note: OpenAssistant Conversations Dataset — fully human-written multi-turn assistant data across thousands of topics. Quality anchoring across business / psychology / advice / general help.

sources.name: openhermes
sources.note: 1M+ broad-coverage instruction examples — sales, marketing, psychology, business advice, motivation, fitness, wealth-building all show up organically. Synthetic (GPT-distilled), highest-quality broad chat dataset on HF.

sources.name: slim-orca
sources.note: 363k diverse instruction examples from the OpenOrca lineage. Synthetic. Strong general-purpose coverage including reasoning + advice + Q&A across professional and personal verticals.

sources.name: ultrachat
sources.note: Multi-turn chat across thousands of topics. Synthetic (ChatGPT-generated). Covers psychology / advice / motivation / business naturally.

sources.name: the-stack-python
sources.note: Real Python from public GitHub.

sources.name: the-stack-typescript
sources.note: TypeScript — Next.js / React / web stack.

sources.name: the-stack-solidity
sources.note: Solidity smart contracts. Web3 / blockchain coverage.

sources.name: the-stack-html
sources.note: HTML markup. Visual-structure vocabulary for UI tasks.

sources.name: the-stack-css
sources.note: CSS / SCSS. Design + layout + Tailwind-adjacent class vocabulary for UI/UX.

sources.name: code-alpaca
sources.note: Code instructions in alpaca format.

sources.name: magicoder-evol
sources.note: 110K evolved code instructions. Highest-quality code SFT on HF.

sources.name: metamath
sources.note: 395K math problems with worked CoT.

sources.name: mathinstruct
sources.note: Hybrid CoT + program-of-thought math instructions.

sources.name: open-platypus
sources.note: STEM reasoning, logic, science. Curated from many sources.

sources.name: ultrainteract
sources.note: Tree-structured CoT reasoning. Strong on real-world problem solving.

sources.name: systemchat
sources.note: Multi-turn dialogues with diverse system prompts. Teaches the model to follow custom personas and instructions cleanly — directly counter-acts robotic 'as an AI' default register.

sources.name: wizardlm-evol
sources.note: 196k evolved instructions across many domains — sales, marketing, psychology, business, technical Q&A. Synthetic but very high quality.

sources.name: the-stack-javascript
sources.note: JavaScript from public GitHub — JSX patterns, React Native components, Node.js. Adds RN production-code vocabulary.
